INFORMATION
WELCOME
At Field Court C of E Infant Academy, our philosophy is to care for, educate and celebrate each child as an individual, building upon their strengths and talents and giving extra support where necessary so that they can experience life in all its fullness. We encourage close links with parents and members of the wider community, believing that a partnership between parents, school and church is the best way to ensure that each child achieves their full potential.
Please click here to access our Admission Policy.
Love Life. Embrace Learning. Believe Together.
This is linked closely to John 10:10 - I may come so that they may have life, and have it to the full.
Information about new vision and the values associated with it can be found here.
Our Core Values drive all that we do and know you will see evidence of them impacting our school should you come and visit us. Our Core Values are: -
Friendship, Courage, Respect, Truthfulness, Forgiveness and Trust.
We are very proud of our recent SIAMS report (March 2020) which it can be read here and our 2023 Ofsted report can be read here.
I hope you find this website useful. The most up-to-date information can be found on our Facebook page (live feed can be found at the bottom of this page), on our newsletters that can be viewed by clicking here, or by contacting Mrs Wright in the school office.
If you would like a paper copy of any of the information on our website please feel free to visit Mrs Wright in the school office and we will be happy to provide it free of charge.
OUR INFANT ACADEMY.
To be truly successful we believe the education of our children must be seen as a partnership between all those concerned; home, pre-school/nursery and school. We consider ourselves very much a ‘family school’ – our children really do enjoy each other’s company. With the Little Explorers situated in the school grounds, we have excellent provision for children aged 2 to 7 all on one site.
LITTLE EXPLORERS.
Our Little Explorers are always busy learning through their play!
For more information about our Nursery or Pre-School setting, please email Mrs Finch at tfinch@fcia.dgat.org.uk
INTERACTIVES
To book places for Before and/or After school club in September, please contact us via email at interactives@fcia.dgat.org.uk
After School Club is always busy! Our children have been filling their afternoons with model building, art work, sports activities, imaginary play and lots more beside.

Christian Character
Field Court C of E Infant Academy Ethos Statement
"Field Court C of E Infant Academy is a school where Christian Values inspire us all to learn in a friendly, vibrant, happy place with the well being of our children, staff and families placed at the heart of everything we do."
As part of the Gloucester Diocese, we use Christian Values as part of our Collective Worship and every day throughout the curriculum. This aims to promote Christian values and understanding throughout all aspects of school life.
Taking a value from a Christian prospective we explore it using Bible stories and stories from different religions to illustrate it.
We sing the Lord’s Prayer at the end of every Collective Worship. It’s a joyful way to finish! Why not sing along? Follow this link....
https://youtu.be/Mu7-UwMIzKs
We also enjoy singing some traditional songs during Worship, such as 'He's Got The Whole World in His Hands'. Join in by following this link...
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vf0mLzNG-lQ
We have a Spiritual Garden which is used for reflection as well as having story time and spending quiet time with our friends. Every one of our classrooms has an area for reflection.
We welcome many visitors, from all cultures, who share their beliefs and experiences with us including Open the Book, Mr Rea (Christian Artist) and Rev'd Mark. We also take time to visit St. James', our Parish Church.
Click here to take a look at St James' Church website.
Christmas at the St James' 2019
Mr Rea is a local church worker, who leads our worship once every six weeks or so. He uses painting and drama to bring alive the Gospel stories in a way that our children can understand, usually involving some of our children in the drama, and interacting with the children to explore what is happening.
The life and teachings of Jesus are taught in a way which ties directly into our own school values and the painting, which he completes during our worship is left behind for display. The key words and depiction of the story in hand remind the children of what was shared, reinforcing the values explored.
Here are a few examples of the stories he has covered recently:
Each month, 6 children from Year 2 attend Eucharist at St James' Church. Here, the children take an active part in the service often reading prayers, preparing the resources and assisting Reverend Jenny.
"I liked taking the candle up."
"Seeing the adults eat the bread was different."
"The wine is meant to be Jesus' blood."
"It's lovely to have the children in the church!"
"They were so well behaved."
Whole School St James' Remembrance Service
Reflection Areas
Each classroom has a Reflection area where we can reflect upon our Christian Values.
Prayers
We believe that everyone should have a voice in our Collective Worship. We therefore invite anyone to write a prayer for us.
If you visit our school, there are prayer hands available in the entrance hall for anyone to write a prayer. Alternatively you can email Mrs Biscoe using admin@fieldcourt-inf.gloucs.sch.uk
We read these prayers during Worship. Sometimes we repeat the prayers as they are timeless. As new ones arrive, they are hung on display in the hall for all to read and take a moment to pause.
Our Christian Values
Our vision is linked closely to John 10:10 - I may come so that they may have life, and have it to the full. Having worked with all of our stakeholders, we voted as a school on our six Core Values. These Core Values drive all that we do and we know you will see evidence of them impacting our school should you come and visit us.
Our Core Values are: -
Friendship, Courage, Respect, Truthfulness, Forgiveness and Trust.
The children and staff explore these during Collective Worship and we ask families to contribute to the Values Tree display in our entrance hall to show how they live out each of our core values on a day-to-day basis.
Values Tree Display
Home School Values
Here are some examples of activities and tasks that are sent home with the children, each term.
Friendship
"Faithful friends are beyond price."
Respect
"Be kind and merciful and forgive others just as God forgave you because of Christ"
Forgiveness
"And you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free."
Courage
"With all your heart you must trust the Lord and not your own judgement."
Truthfulness
"And you will know the truth, and the truth will set you free."
Trust
"With all your heart you must trust the Lord and not your own judgement."

Our Spiritual Garden
Our Spiritual garden
Over recent years, there has been a move for many schools to consider redesigning their outdoor space to facilitate a variety of functions. In many church schools this has included areas to encourage pupils to reflect, find quiet and calm and to allow for prayer, reflection and peer mediation.
Our Spiritual Garden is used for spending time with our friends in quiet reflection. We often use the garden for Story Time where we enjoy sharing tales from the bible as we are lucky enough to have it of a size where we can enjoy collective class worship.
Each year group has their own planting area where we can learn how to grown our own vegetables and herbs.
We welcome many visitors, from all cultures, who share their beliefs and experiences with us, including the Open the Book team, Pastor Tom Geatches and Father John from St.James Church.

PLEASE NOTE
Parents are requested not to use the staff car park when collecting or dropping off their children. Please observe the parking restrictions outside the school.
Access is by the smaller gate nearest the Infant school entrance. Please ring the bell to be let in. The gate is on a magnetic catch, please pull once the gate has been released.

PRICING & PAYMENT
The Breakfast Club is priced at £5.00 per child for each session, with a 10% reduction for siblings attending the same session.
Breakfast Club runs term time only ie only on the mornings of the days that school is open. It is open to children who attend our school, Little Explorers and Years 3 or 4 of Field Court Junior Academy.
In order to register, please email interactives@fcia.dgat.org.uk letting us know the mornings you wish to attend. We will send you a googleform to complete before setting an account up for you on School Money. School Money is the online booking system that we use for you to book and pay for sessions. All sessions are to be booked in advance to ensure availability and, more importantly, the safety of the children by knowing which sessions they are due to attend. More information will be sent to you when your place has been confirmed.

PARENTS' PAGES
Little Explorers offer a stimulating, secure and caring environment where children are valued and treated as individuals. We encourage children to develop their language skills, mathematical thinking and help build their natural curiosity for the world around them. Children are encouraged to be creative, enjoy physical play and to develop positive social relationship with adults and children.
Children learn best through play and at Little Explorers we understand the need for children to be able to engage in exciting activities that allow them to develop their own ideas and thoughts, whilst being supported by motivated and enthusiastic adults.
All of the team at Little Explorers are passionate about Early Years childcare and the concept of learning through play. Between us we have over 40 years experience of caring for young children at a professional level, and pride ourselves on the quality of our work. We hope that children and parents alike find us friendly.

LITTLE EXPLORERS
PARENTS' PAGES
Little Explorers offer a stimulating, secure and caring environment where children are valued and treated as individuals. We encourage children to develop their language skills, mathematical thinking and help build their natural curiosity for the world around them. Children are encouraged to be creative, enjoy physical play and to develop positive social relationship with adults and children.
Children learn best through play and at Little Explorers we understand the need for children to be able to engage in exciting activities that allow them to develop their own ideas and thoughts, whilst being supported by motivated and enthusiastic adults.
All of the team at Little Explorers are passionate about Early Years childcare and the concept of learning through play. Between us we have over 40 years experience of caring for young children at a professional level, and pride ourselves on the quality of our work. We hope that children and parents alike find us friendly.
